???+ remember "Before you start, remember"

    ??? question "What is `square(4.0)` an example of, and what happens when it runs?"

        A function call. The function's body runs, then execution carries on from just after the call.

        Introduced in [Learn: 5. Expressions](../../language-tour/08-expressions.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../../specification/expressions.md#calls).

    ??? question "What does `fn add(left: i32, right: i32) -> i32 { ... }` declare, and when does its body run?"

        A function. Its body runs only when code calls it, or, for `main`, when the program starts.

        Introduced in [Learn: 7. Declarations](../../language-tour/10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../../specification/declarations.md#32-functions).

    ??? question "What do we call a variable declared with `let` inside a function?"

        A local variable. It needs an initializer and is visible from its declaration to the end of its block.

        Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../../specification/declarations.md#35-local-variable-declarations).

    ??? question "What is one basic operation a processor can carry out, such as adding two numbers, called?"

        An instruction. Machine code is a sequence of instructions in numeric form.

        Introduced in [6. The first machine code](stage-6-first-machine-code.md).

    ??? question "In the call `add(3, 4)`, what are `3` and `4` called?"

        Arguments. Each one supplies the value for one parameter, and their number and types must match the parameter list.

        Introduced in [Learn: 7. Declarations](../../language-tour/10-declarations.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../../specification/expressions.md#calls).
